correctness.rationale: For any finite factor, alternating shadowed x/y successor existential quantifiers express its occurrence with FO²; arbitrary factor-language equality forces equality of primitive periodic necklaces by finite-residue pigeonholing. A definable length-d factor T_u(x) selects one primitive residue per repetition, detecting k>=2; nonadjacent opposite-colour witnesses separate k=2/3 when d=2, and loops, bidirected edges and nonneighbors separate k=1/2/3/4 when d=1. At k>=c(d), preserving primitive residue and equality/both successor atoms gives the full finite two-pebble back-and-forth: the equal, forward, backward, and nonneighbor options exist with the same residues exactly from k=4,3,2 in the respective three regimes. Thus arbitrary-rank equivalence is proved, including length-one loops and length-two bidirected cases. Independent semantic partition computation compared 101 colored-cycle models and 80 predicted equivalence classes with zero disagreements. The bounded computation corroborates but does not establish the universal quantification.
